newsitem.title: INDIA: India 3-day money at 3.5 pct, SBI resumes lending.
newsitem.headline: India 3-day money at 3.5 pct, SBI resumes lending.

text.p: The inter-bank call money market was inactive on Friday, the banks' reporting day, dealers said.
Three-day money was quoted at 3.25-3.75 percent, with stray deals at 3.50 percent, one dealer said.
The state-run Andhra Bank said it struck a deal for three month money at 7.25 percent.
The State Bank of India (SBI) resumed lending in the call market on Thursday afternoon and transacted an estimated business of over 7.0 billion rupees, dealers said.
At Thursday's repo auction, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised 45.50 billion rupees, a quantum jump from 11.0 billion rupees raised at the June 16 auction.
Money market dealers said SBI accounted for the lion's share of subscription at the repo auction.
SBI could not participate at the last two repo auctions because of a strike at its Bombay office.
Some dealers said SBI accounted for almost 30.0 billion rupees at Thursday's repo auction.
"Despite SBI's absence, call did not shoot up," said a money market manager at a foreign bank. With SBI resuming its lending operations, call is expected to be soft next week.
Call rates are widely expected to open at 5.0-5.5 percent level on Saturday, the first day of the new fortnight.
The RBI is conducting two auctions on Friday for 91-day and 14-day treasury bills.
